label: provisional
paradigm: These criteria serve a buyer choosing what to purchase, new or pre-owned: an evidence-based, value-aware buyer who wants an informed view of history and context. They are one reasonable buyer's stance, not the only one, and this version is provisional: drafted from published sources, not yet compiled or ratified.

change_log.reason: Drafted from Monochrome's and Fratello's technical guides to office versus traveller's GMT watches, Timex's water-resistance ratings and Gear Patrol on fit. The Teddy content audit of 2026-11-14 covers no GMT-specific principle, so none is seeded.

spec_fields.complications: list of lower-case strings, for example "date", "chronograph", "gmt"; [] for time only
spec_fields.water_resistance_m: number: rated water resistance in metres

wearer.statement: How the buyer uses a second zone decides the type: a traveller who resets local time on arrival wants a flyer (traveller's) GMT; someone at home tracking a distant office or family is served as well by a caller (office) GMT.
The watch fits the buyer's wrist: lug-to-lug length inside the flat top of the wrist and a thickness the buyer's cuffs and comfort allow. Measure these rather than trusting the stated diameter.
wearer.test: Compare the stated lug-to-lug length with the buyer's measured flat wrist width; try the watch on where possible.

watch.statement: The watch shows a second time zone on a 24-hour scale (a GMT hand or equivalent).

For travel: the local hour hand jumps in one-hour steps, forwards and backwards, without stopping the watch or disturbing the home-time hand (a flyer or 'true' GMT). An office GMT sets the 24-hour hand instead and needs the time stopped to change local time.

How the date behaves when local time is changed: on a traveller's GMT moving the hour hand backwards affects the date and may need correcting; on an office GMT the date is usually set separately in one direction.
A rotating 24-hour bezel adds a third time zone. Useful, but a bonus rather than the core of the function.
At least 50 m (light swimming in a brand's ratings), so a travel watch can stay on at the pool or beach. This links the brand ratings to travel use; no GMT source sets it.

principles_note: Teddy's principles are quoted from the videos' auto-captions (wording as captioned), located by text search of the caption track; timestamps are the caption segment where the quote begins. They enter as practitioner consensus, never as standards. His videos state his store is an authorized dealer for over 35 brands.
